_comment: Verification manifest for the review of PR #402 (a DOCUMENTATION PR: doc/best-practice/{zh,en}/05-port-allocation-and-service-discovery{,-guide}.md). Consumed by scripts/re-verify.sh. Every finding is a DOC defect: the implementation is the source of truth. Polarity semantics here: 'contract' tests pin the real implementation behaviour and stay GREEN after the doc is corrected; 'canary' tests pin CURRENT CODE behaviour that the doc contradicts, so they FLIP RED only if the maintainers change the CODE instead of the DOC.

live._note: Needs the controller started with --enable-port-allocator=true. Creates a scoped namespace and deletes it on exit.

findings.claim: references can only resolve PodScoped ports. A RoleScoped target hard-fails with 'referenced port not found: prefill.leader.leader-grpc (key: <pod>.leader-grpc)' and blocks Pod creation. The doc (zh:313-344 / en:316-347) implies any already-allocated port of another component in the same role resolves, with no scope constraint.

random port allocation is NOT unique across AllocateBatch calls (random.go:28-31), and PodScoped allocation calls AllocateBatch once per Pod; Release() is a no-op with zero bookkeeping. The doc (zh:222-245 / en:225-248, zh:278) presents dynamic allocation as the fix for hostNetwork port collisions.

the LEADER_ADDR / WORKER_*_ADDR examples at zh:597/606/614/616/618 and en:600/609/617/619/621 are ellipsis-truncated into illegal FQDNs, and the three router table rows collapse to one byte-identical string. The real format is <instanceName>-<component>-<index>.<svcName>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local (component_discovery.go:140-141).
findings.note: Round 2: confirmed against real Pods / a real ConfigMap, not just unit level.

findings.claim: the guide's /etc/rbg/config.yaml listing at zh:183-208 / en:184-209 prints size before roles and size before instances, but the payload is produced by sigs.k8s.io/yaml (config_builder.go:91), which emits mapping keys ALPHABETICALLY: group -> name,roles,size; per role -> instances,size; the roles map sorted decode-before-prefill. The same guide prints the CORRECT alphabetical order at zh:228-239.
findings.note: Round 2: confirmed against real Pods / a real ConfigMap, not just unit level.

findings.claim: zh:32-38 / en:33-39 state the Service naming rule unconditionally as s-{rbgName}-{roleName}. GetCompatibleHeadlessServiceName (pkg/utils/service_utils.go:30-45) keeps the LEGACY {rbgName}-{roleName} name when such a Service already exists, and GetServiceName (api/workloads/v1alpha2/helper.go:106-116) truncates at 63 chars and strips a trailing hyphen.

en:666 renders 'In-Place Update and In-Place Scheduling' as plain text rather than a link. VERIFIED CORRECT: doc/best-practice/en/04-* does not exist (only 01,02,03,05,10 are present), so the author deliberately avoided a dead link. No test required; checked by `ls doc/best-practice/en/`.

Positive baseline measured on real Pods: 6 RBG_* env vars on a standalone role (exactly the base+Stateful+RoleInstanceSet sub-tables, RBG_LWP_* absent as the doc's split implies), hostname/subdomain identity, rbg-cluster-config mounted read-only at /etc/rbg, headless Services s-a-prefill / s-pd-prefill with clusterIP None and publishNotReadyAddresses true, group.size = role count (1) distinct from roles.<r>.size = replicas (2), allocated port 31349 inside 30000-34999, and the four portAllocator flags reaching /manager.

liveNote: Round 2 (2026-08-05): the live layer is now available. The blocker was a controller-image lag -- the cluster ran v0.8.0-cea2a47 (commit cea2a472, 23 commits behind main, older than #394) which wrote restartPolicy as a bare string while the already-correct CRDs required an object, so no Pod was ever created. Fixed with: helm upgrade rbgs deploy/helm/rbgs -n rbg-system --set controller.features.portAllocator.enabled=true (chart 0.8.0-alpha.3, image rolebasedgroup/rbgs-controller:v0.8.0-47cfe17). Cluster: v1.36.1-aliyun.1, 3 nodes. No data migration was needed because the cluster held zero RoleInstanceSets -- do not assume that next time. Both round-1 environment limits are gone: Pods start, and the controller now runs with --enable-port-allocator=true --port-allocate-strategy=random --start-port=30000 --port-range=5000. F3 and F4 are confirmed live. F1, F2 and F5 stay unit-level on purpose: F2 rests on the pigeonhole principle (9 PodScoped ports out of a range of 8 makes a duplicate certain), which is exact, whereas provoking a collision in a 5000-port range live would be flaky; F5 needs a pre-existing legacy-named Service, so the live run only covers the no-legacy branch. IMPORTANT: the live run allocates one port on one component, so it is NOT evidence that allocation is collision-free -- F2 stands.
